text:
Yes, the conviction should be reversed, because the evidence showed the patient would have died before long regardless, so the defective drug was not shown to be a but-for cause of death; at most it accelerated an inevitable death, which generally supports a lesser homicide charge rather than murder. Murder also requires proof of intent to kill, and a manufacturer who ships a substandard lot for business reasons is violating a product-quality rule, not acting with homicidal intent.
CONFIDENCE: 85
